Histograms of drawing and contour properties

Source: R/statistics.R
contour_statistics.Rd

Orientation, curvature and horizontal/vertical histograms are weighted by segment length. Length histograms collect total contour length. Junctions count events; per-contour junctions count each participating contour once. MAT histograms count mapped pixels, including valid zero scores. Values outside the logarithmic range enter the first/last bin. Orientation is axial; exact bin boundaries enter the upper bin, including odd bin counts.

Usage

contour_statistics(
  x,
  properties = c("orientation", "length", "curvature", "horizontal_vertical",
    "junction_type", "junction_angle"),
  bins = 8,
  by = c("drawing", "contour"),
  normalize = FALSE,
  length_range = c(2, max(3, x$width + x$height)),
  curvature_range = c(0, 90),
  spec = x$feature_spec,
  pixels_per_degree = NULL,
  estimator = c("turning", "mlv2023")
)

Arguments

x

A drawing.

properties

Property names.

bins

Positive number of bins (junction types always have five).

by

Summarize the drawing or each contour.

normalize

Scale by contour length to units per 10,000 pixels.

length_range, curvature_range

Increasing nonnegative log-bin ranges.

spec

Optional feature specification, exclusive of individual feature settings. Enriched drawings use their saved specification by default.

pixels_per_degree

Optional input calibration override.

estimator

Curvature definition without a specification: vertex turning (default) or the published `"mlv2023"` estimator.

Value

A long data frame with bin boundaries, centers, values and units.

Details

A value that differs from a bin edge by at most 1e-9 x max(1, |edge|) is binned as if it lay exactly on the edge, in the coordinate in which the bins are equally spaced (degrees for orientation and junction angles, log10(1 + x) for length and the published curvature, the raw value otherwise). Angles that are mathematically equal, such as a computed 59.999999999999993 and an exact 60 degrees, therefore share a bin on every platform. Rounding residue is many orders of magnitude smaller than this tolerance, and real measurement differences many orders larger.

Without a specification, curvature uses the vertex turning estimator (`estimator = "turning"`): each vertex turn is spread uniformly over its dual cell, half of each adjacent segment, so every turn is counted once. The published estimator, `estimator = "mlv2023"`, assigns each segment the turn to its neighbour divided by its own length and so counts every corner twice; see [feature_spec()].
